skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest X-ray for radiological signs of chronic pulmonary embolism or pulmonary hypertension.
steps: Assess the size and contour of the main and hilar pulmonary arteries; look for enlargement (prominence) which suggests elevated pulmonary pressure.
Evaluate the cardiac silhouette, specifically the right heart border and apex, for evidence of right ventricular hypertrophy or enlargement.

Distinguish between options by correlating findings: if pulmonary arteries are normal in caliber and the right ventricle is not enlarged, findings are inconsistent with significant pulmonary hypertension secondary to chronic PE.
